issue.title: `onDownloadProgress` never emits `percent: 1` for empty response bodies

arms.better: The agent located and edited the right transform quickly, and the merged stream regression tests passed against its implementation. However, `tm ticket new` printed `Created ticket T-1: ...` to stdout; treating that whole line as the ticket ID made the prescribed shell sequence fail with a parser error, so a machine-readable ID/output mode would avoid user guesswork. The run then retried into provider 429 failures and ended escalated after editing the implementation; its failure report offered retry/resume guidance but no successful final handoff or trustworthy verification report. The event payload exposed a diagnostic claiming 170,893 tokens for a stalled attempt plus 12,638 recorded tokens on the final failed attempt, so usage reporting could be clearer. Mechanically, `npx ava test/stream.ts` passed 19/19 after hidden-test overwrite, but the required `pnpm test` failed in XO on the untouched `test/http-error.ts:218` (`no-meaningless-void-operator`); browser tests also could not launch because Playwright browser binaries were not installed.

The agent reached `source/utils/body.ts` quickly, implemented the flush behavior, added a focused empty-body regression test, and ran `npx ava test/stream.ts` with 18 passing tests before giving a concise, accurate result. Its initial glob missed tests, but it corrected course by searching for the progress test and then editing the right file; it could improve context efficiency slightly by using the exact task and existing test layout earlier. The hidden merged stream tests passed after overwrite (`npx ava test/stream.ts`: 19/19), but the required `pnpm test` verification failed at XO on the pre-existing untouched `test/http-error.ts:218` rule violation, and `npx ava test/browser.ts` could not complete because Playwright browser binaries were not installed.
